children: A group of 13 Democratic senators led by Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (Ore.) has launched an investigation into whether health insurers colluded with President Trump in removing about 760K individuals from health insurance marketplace coverage.
In September, the Trump administration announced the
The senators sent letters to 10 of the largest insurers, including Cigna
, with questions regarding their involvement in removing members from coverage, including the companies' interaction with CMS.
The lawmakers claim that the insurers sent members unsolicited communications. If individuals failed to respond, they were deemed fraudulent, and their coverage was cancelled.

"We have many questions about the role of Cigna in this flawed process used to terminate coverage for 760,000 enrollees, and the judgment exercised by insurance companies that chose to cooperate with CMS officials without requesting clarification about the specific authorities being relied on to support this request or raising concerns to Congress on behalf of their customers, enrollees that your companies receive billions of dollars in premiums and taxpayer support each year to serve," the letter to Cigna states.

title: Senate Democrats probe whether health insurers involved with ACA purge
